method: Feature-detected task transport; controlled native postTask promise+AbortSignal emulator and timer queues, integrated with otherwise byte-identical production exact-anchor job/slice logic. Node default/global detection also exercised. Not native Chrome timing.

checks.name: Supported environment posts an asynchronous user-visible task with an AbortSignal and no timer
Native cancellation aborts its promise and a forced late callback is inert
No native API and no AbortController independently use cancellable Node-compatible timers
Synchronous native scheduling failure falls back once and remains cancellable
Native rejection before callback falls back once without unhandled rejection
Cancel after native rejection cancels its fallback task too
An AbortError not caused by our cancellation cannot silently strand the job
Callback exceptions are reported as task errors and never invoke callback twice
A returned callback rejection is reported once and never treated as native scheduling failure
Exact scheduler retains identical complete results and slice boundaries with native and timer scheduling
Native pending generation is aborted on supersede and cannot commit after the new result
Native destroy and failed context both leave no commits or unhandled abort promises
Production default feature-detects global scheduler rather than requiring injection
No unhandled promise rejection occurred in any cancellation, failure or callback case
